Confirmed via stash-bisection this reproduces at pure dev baseline with zero task changes present (tests/test_bff_main_composition.py, an existing file, already does a qualified import and triggers it against tests/test_management_read_models_router.py) -- a genuine pre-existing defect, not introduced by this task.
gap_B_evidence_route_cross_test_contamin.fix: test_bff_promotion_review_governance.py previously made this worse by installing the same alias unconditionally at file-collection time (module-level `sys.modules.setdefault(...)`, not scoped to _isolated_client()). Scoped it to _isolated_client()'s lifetime instead: save whatever was previously registered under the qualified key on entry, install the alias only for the context manager's duration, and restore the original entry (or remove it if absent) in `finally`, mirroring the existing read_store/command_store/persona_service restore pattern already in that function. This removes this task's governance test file as a contributor.

Re-running tests/test_management_read_timeout_and_capacity.py + tests/test_management_read_models_router.py together (after the scoping fix above) still reproduces the same 2 evidence-route failures, confirming the underlying pre-existing defect in _resolve_evidence_reader persists via this and other already-existing qualified-import test files regardless of this task's fix. gap_2_get_human_inbox_had_no_per_contrib.root_cause: management_read_models/service.py::get_human_inbox's persona_readiness contributor (block 5) called store.list_personas() directly and inline -- no timeout, no capacity, and it did not go through _build_persona_readiness_items at all, so the only bound that existed was the single whole-route offload from defect 2's fix (a necessary but insufficient bound per the acceptance criteria: it cannot produce a persona_readiness-specific read_timeout/read_capacity_saturated reason while sibling contributors stay populated).
gap_2_get_human_inbox_had_no_per_contrib.fix: Added main.py::_bounded_human_inbox_persona_readiness(snapshot_at, read_store=...) -- a plain concurrent.futures bound (capacity.acquire(blocking=False) + executor.submit + future.result(timeout=...)) around the existing, patchable _build_persona_readiness_items, reusing the existing _HUMAN_INBOX_READ_SLOTS/_HUMAN_INBOX_READ_EXECUTOR pool and _human_inbox_surface_timeout_seconds() budget (not a new pool). A plain synchronous bound (not the asyncio run_management_read) was required because callers include already-synchronous code paths on the request thread (ManagementService.get_hiq_backlog and get_management_cockpit both call get_human_inbox() inline; hiq-backlog's route is not even offloaded, so it runs on the FastAPI event-loop thread where asyncio.run() would raise). Added ManagementService._bounded_persona_readiness_rows, which delegates to main.py's helper (live sys.modules lookup, same pattern as every other main-owned seam in this file) and falls back to an inline, unbounded call only when main.py isn't the live composition root. Rewired get_human_inbox's persona_readiness block (5) to use it, producing surfaces['persona_readiness']={status:degraded, reason: read_timeout|read_capacity_saturated} + meta.partial=True on degradation, exactly like every sibling contributor block already does, while approvals/governance/interventions/sentinel/promotion_reviews stay unaffected.
gap_2_get_human_inbox_had_no_per_contrib.critical_wiring_correction: The whole-route run_management_read(svc.get_human_inbox, ...) offload (defect 2's fix) also dispatched by function-name match on "human_inbox" to the *same* _HUMAN_INBOX_READ_SLOTS pool the new persona_readiness contributor now uses. Nesting the identical non-reentrant BoundedSemaphore at both the whole-route level and the per-contributor level inside it meant the outer acquire permanently starved the inner one (0 capacity remaining by the time the contributor tried to acquire, on every call, regardless of real load). Fixed by special-casing the whole-route dispatch (name in {"get_human_inbox", "_bounded_get_human_inbox" -- the latter being router.py's own class-level timeout-proxy wrapper of ManagementService.get_human_inbox}) to the generic _MANAGEMENT_READ_DEFAULT_SLOTS pool instead, reserving _HUMAN_INBOX_READ_SLOTS exclusively for the real per-contributor bound. Verified this does not regress the pre-existing whole-route capacity-saturation test (tests/test_management_read_timeout_and_capacity.py::test_human_inbox_capacity_saturation_yields_immediate_degraded_response_and_recovers), which still passes because saturating the persona_readiness leaf bound now produces the same observable whole-route degradation that test asserts on.

defect_2_unbounded_capacity.root_cause: _dep("run_management_read") resolved to main.py's re-exported personas.routes.common.run_management_read with no capacity/executor bound -- capacity=None means an unbounded asyncio.to_thread fan-out for every one of the 17 Management-read routes (cockpit, human-inbox, hiq-backlog, evidence, etc.).
defect_2_unbounded_capacity.fix: main.py now defines named, bounded capacity pools mirroring the existing _MANAGEMENT_DATA_SOURCES_READ_SLOTS pattern: _HUMAN_INBOX_READ_SLOTS / _HUMAN_INBOX_READ_EXECUTOR, _MANAGEMENT_COCKPIT_READ_SLOTS / _MANAGEMENT_COCKPIT_READ_EXECUTOR, and _MANAGEMENT_READ_DEFAULT_SLOTS / _MANAGEMENT_READ_DEFAULT_EXECUTOR (default pool for every other management/governance read). main.py's run_management_read now wraps the raw personas.routes.common.run_management_read, dispatching to the correct named pool by the offloaded callable's __name__ when the caller does not already pass an explicit capacity/executor (existing explicit callers, e.g. the Source Ingest registry read, are unaffected). This is the real composition-root run_management_read every create_management_router()/create_*_router() call site in app_factory.py already resolves via _dep("run_management_read").
defect_2_unbounded_capacity.scope_not_completed: The task brief's acceptance criteria describe a more granular per-contributor timeout story: a single human-inbox surface (e.g. persona_readiness) timing out independently with meta.partial=True while sibling surfaces remain populated, and a distinct 'read_capacity_saturated' reason string. Tracing the real /bff/management/human-inbox route (management_read_models/service.py::get_human_inbox) shows each of its 6 contributor blocks reads synchronously and inline with no per-contributor async offload, timeout, or meta.partial computation at all -- only the whole get_human_inbox call is offloaded/bounded as one unit (which is what this fix bounds). Building genuine per-contributor bounded/timeout semantics is a materially larger, separate feature and was not implemented. The two most elaborate tests in test_bff_promotion_review_governance.py that assume this finer-grained architecture (test_human_inbox_capacity_prevents_late_queue_and_bounds_cockpit_hiq_overlap, test_cockpit_composition_timeout_does_not_block_event_loop) still fail for this reason; they also reference a hook function (bff_main._build_management_cockpit_payload) that does not exist anywhere in production.
